subject: EdgeFlow live endpoint — sustained chunk silence during high QPS
raw_thread:
<Email 1>
From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@edgeflow.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeFlow SRE <support@edgeflow.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Live endpoint: repeated silent chunks under burst traffic

David,

We started load testing a new route at ~750 qps at 08:00 PST and are seeing long stretches (5–12s) where the WebSocket stream returns no token chunks. The client reports "complete response" but then nothing for multiple seconds; when that happens we see token emission resume without warning. This is impacting latency SLAs and causing retries from our clients.

I've attached a small PCAP and a token-heatmap CSV captured from our client. This is happening across both the us-east and us-west endpoints for you.

Can you confirm whether this is something on our side or if the Redwood runtime is dropping/choking chunked transfer? We also included a short screenshot of token-rate metrics.

Thanks,
Ravi
SRE, EdgeFlow

Attachments: edgeflow-live-pcap.txt (text stub), edgeflow-token-heatmap.csv (csv stub), metrics_snapshot.png (image stub)

Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Live endpoint: repeated silent chunks under burst traffic

Quick technical update:

I pulled runtime logs for the affected time window. Findings:
- Proxy worker queues show sustained queue depth spikes (queue_length > 300) during the reported bursts.
- Heartbeat frames (WS ping/pong) were exchanged but we still saw absence of data frames for up to 10 seconds.
- Kernel-level preemption events coincide with the queue spikes — likely due to noisy-neighbor scheduling on the host.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Isolated a suspect host and drained traffic off it to rule out a bad network NIC.
2) Increased proxy worker threads for the affected pool and disabled aggressive coalescing on the proxy's Nagle-like buffer.
3) Enabled a short-term client-side keepalive patch to surface stalls faster to callers.

EdgeFlow: can you reproduce after 09:15? Also please confirm whether you saw client-side TCP retransmits.

-Rishi

Ravi,

Follow-up after 24h of monitoring:
- We confirmed queue-coalescing on the proxy as the primary contributor. Rolling back that optimization eliminated multi-second silent stretches in our canary pool.
- We identified a scheduling hotspot and applied a short-term host affinity change; long-term fix is a scheduler-level fairness tweak scheduled for next week.
- No client-side TCP retransmit patterns beyond expected levels.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem draft will be shared by Monday with timeline and RCA.
2) CS: Vanessa, please issue the 10% credit as discussed and include an apology note and the mitigation summary.
3) We'll run a joint load test with EdgeFlow under a controlled surge and provide telemetry.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we'll keep monitoring closely.

—David
